# pulse_builtin_alert_rule (Resource)

Settings of one of Pulse's built-in alert rules. Built-in rules always exist; this resource manages their settings. Unset attributes take the rule's built-in defaults, and destroying the resource puts all of them back (the rule itself stays). Declare each `kind` at most once. Import with the kind, e.g. `backup_stale`.

Built-in defaults (every rule is enabled by default):

| kind | severity | for_seconds | params |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backup_stale` | `critical` | 0 | `hours = 36` |
| `ban_storm` | `warning` | 0 | `count = 10`, `window_minutes = 10` |
| `cert_expiry` | `critical` | 0 | `days = 14` |
| `client_expiry` | `warning` | 0 | `days = 30` |
| `dead_letters` | `warning` | 0 | `hours = 24` |
| `disk_forecast` | `warning` | 0 | `days = 30` |
| `nats_down` | `critical` | 60 | none |
| `slow_consumers` | `warning` | 0 | `window_minutes = 10` |
| `stream_usage` | `warning` | 0 | `ratio = 0.85` |

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Backups run nightly: alert after two missed nights instead of the default 36 hours.
resource "pulse_builtin_alert_rule" "backup_stale" {
  kind   = "backup_stale"
  params = { hours = 50 }
}

# Certificates renew 30 days ahead; only a warning when 7 days are left.
resource "pulse_builtin_alert_rule" "cert_expiry" {
  kind     = "cert_expiry"
  severity = "warning"
  params   = { days = 7 }
}

# No interest in slow consumer notices.
resource "pulse_builtin_alert_rule" "slow_consumers" {
  kind    = "slow_consumers"
  enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) Which built-in rule: `backup_stale`, `ban_storm`, `cert_expiry`, `client_expiry`, `dead_letters`, `disk_forecast`, `nats_down`, `slow_consumers`, `stream_usage`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Disabled rules are not evaluated; disabling one resolves its alerts without notifications. Default `true`.
- `for_seconds` (Number) How long the condition must hold before the alert fires, in seconds (at most 604800). Defaults to the rule's built-in value.
- `params` (Attributes) The rule's thresholds. Each kind uses only some of them (see the table above); setting another is an error. Unset ones take the built-in defaults; the ones the kind does not use stay null. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params))
- `severity` (String) `info`, `warning` or `critical`. Defaults to the rule's built-in severity.

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) What the rule checks.
- `id` (String) Rule ID (the same as `kind`).
- `name` (String) Rule name shown in notifications.

<a id="nestedatt--params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params`

Optional:

- `count` (Number) `ban_storm`: number of bans within `window_minutes` (at least 1).
- `days` (Number) `disk_forecast`: fire when a stream reaches its size limit within this many days at the current rate. `cert_expiry`, `client_expiry`: fire when less than this many days are left. Positive.
- `hours` (Number) `backup_stale`: fire when no backup succeeded for this many hours. `dead_letters`: look-back window in hours. Positive.
- `ratio` (Number) `stream_usage`: fire above this fraction of a stream's size limit (between 0 and 1).
- `window_minutes` (Number) `ban_storm`, `slow_consumers`: evaluation window in minutes (at least 1).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the rule kind.
terraform import pulse_builtin_alert_rule.backup_stale backup_stale
```
